✓ Calque.fact: In linguistics, a calque () or loan translation is a word or phrase borrowed from another language by literal word-for-word or root-for-root translation. When used as a verb, "to calque" means to borrow a word or phrase from another language while translating its components, so as to create a new word or phrase (lexeme) in the target language.

✓ Calque.subject: General Science

For example, the name of the Irish digital television service Saorview is a partial calque of that of the UK service "Freeview", translating the first half of the word from English to Irish but leaving the second half unchanged.

✓ Citric acid cycle.question: The _____ was Interconnected biochemical reactions releasing energy.
✓ Citric acid cycle.fact: The citric acid cycle—also called the Krebs cycle, Szent–Györgyi–Krebs cycle, or TCA cycle (tricarboxylic acid cycle)—is a series of biochemical reactions that release the energy stored in nutrients through acetyl-CoA oxidation.

✓ Citric acid cycle.subject: General Science
✓ Citric acid cycle.question: The cycle consumes acetate (in the form of acetyl-CoA) and water and reduces NAD+ to _____, releasing carbon dioxide
✓ Citric acid cycle.fact: The cycle consumes acetate (in the form of acetyl-CoA) and water and reduces NAD+ to NADH, releasing carbon dioxide. The NADH generated by the citric acid cycle is fed into the oxidative phosphorylation (electron transport) pathway.

✓ Citric acid cycle.subject: General Science
✓ Citric acid cycle.question: Independently citric acid cycle was identified in _____ by German biochemists Carl Martius and Franz Knoop
✓ Citric acid cycle.fact: The citric acid cycle itself was finally identified in 1937 by Hans Adolf Krebs and William Arthur Johnson while at the University of Sheffield, for which the former received the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine in 1953, and for whom the cycle is sometimes named the "Krebs cycle". Independently citric acid cycle was identified in 1937 by German biochemists Carl Martius and Franz Knoop.

✓ Citric acid cycle.subject: General Science
✓ Citric acid cycle.question: Most of the electrons made available by the oxidative steps of the cycle are transferred to NAD+, forming _____
✓ Citric acid cycle.fact: Most of the electrons made available by the oxidative steps of the cycle are transferred to NAD+, forming NADH. For each acetyl group that enters the citric acid cycle, three molecules of NADH are produced.

✓ Citric acid cycle.subject: General Science
✓ Citric acid cycle.question: Two carbon atoms are oxidized to CO2, the energy from these reactions is transferred to other metabolic processes through GTP (or ATP), and as electrons in _____ and QH2
✓ Citric acid cycle.fact: For every NADH and FADH2 that are produced in the citric acid cycle, 2.5 and 1.5 ATP molecules are generated in oxidative phosphorylation, respectively. Two carbon atoms are oxidized to CO2, the energy from these reactions is transferred to other metabolic processes through GTP (or ATP), and as electrons in NADH and QH2.

✓ Citric acid cycle.subject: General Science
✓ Citric acid cycle.question: Therefore, at the end of two cycles, the products are: two GTP, six _____, two FADH2, and four CO2
✓ Citric acid cycle.fact: Therefore, at the end of two cycles, the products are: two GTP, six NADH, two FADH2, and four CO2. In eukaryotes, two equivalents of NADH and two equivalents of ATP are generated in glycolysis, which takes place in the cytoplasm.

✓ Citric acid cycle.subject: General Science
✓ Citric acid cycle.question: In eukaryotes, two equivalents of _____ and two equivalents of ATP are generated in glycolysis, which takes place in the cytoplasm
✓ Citric acid cycle.fact: Therefore, at the end of two cycles, the products are: two GTP, six NADH, two FADH2, and four CO2. In eukaryotes, two equivalents of NADH and two equivalents of ATP are generated in glycolysis, which takes place in the cytoplasm.

✓ Citric acid cycle.subject: General Science
✓ Citric acid cycle.question: The observed yields are, therefore, closer to ~2.5 ATP per _____ and ~1.5 ATP per FADH2, further reducing the total net production of ATP to approximately 30
✓ Citric acid cycle.fact: In eukaryotes, two equivalents of NADH and two equivalents of ATP are generated in glycolysis, which takes place in the cytoplasm. If transported using the glycerol phosphate shuttle rather than the malate–aspartate shuttle, transport of two of these equivalents of NADH into the mitochondria effectively consumes two equivalents of ATP, thus reducing the net production of ATP to 36.
